## Recommendation
- Fish the Grand Haven pier. I'd expect a rating of 1 (below average) there, the best of the four.
- Expect slow pier fishing at St. Joseph (0) and only a below-average chance at South Haven and Muskegon (about 1, low confidence). Those ports have no recent pier-specific salmon report.
- If you go, fish early morning with glow spoons. That is the only pier method the reports mention.
- Don't count on the pier. Boat anglers have had better results, and that's worth checking if you can get out.

## Why
- Grand Haven's pier reports range from slow to below average, and only Grand Haven had any pier catches this month (Grand Haven, 2023-09-20 and 2023-09-13).
- The most recent Grand Haven pier report was slow, and it came from the same week as the boat reports (Grand Haven, 2023-09-27).
- I'd expect the warm water to keep pier action slow. The satellite reading at the Grand Haven pierhead was about 67 F and flat, with no upwelling in the last three days, and salmon usually prefer 52-58 F (Michigan Sea Grant; Grand Haven, 2023-09-27 and the conditions summary).
- St. Joseph's only pier salmon report this season was slow (St. Joseph, 2023-08-30), and early-October pier reports from 2022 were also slow (St. Joseph, 2022-10-05).

## Evidence
**Recent reports (newest is 6 days old; Muskegon's is 27 days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-27: pier slow, "A couple were caught early in the morning while casting glow spoons." (quality 0)
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-20: pier below average, "caught a few salmon while casting glow spoons early in the morning." (quality 1)
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-13: pier Chinook and coho on glow spoons, quality 1 for Chinook (coho not rated). Boats did much better, rated 4 on glow J-plugs and white flies.
- Grand Haven, 2023-09-06: pier slow on glow spoons (quality 0).
- Muskegon, 2023-09-06: pier slow on glow spoons (quality 0). No newer Muskegon salmon report.
- South Haven, 2023-09-27: boats slow, river slow. The only pier-relevant entry is a 2023-09-13 spoon catch rated 1 with the access type unknown.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-30: pier slow for trout and salmon (quality 0). The 2023-09-27 St. Joseph report covered boats and river only, with boats slow.

**Past seasons (general guidance from history, not this week's reports)**
- Similar water temperatures in past years (within 4 F of 66 F) gave slow pier reports at St. Joseph (2022-10-05) and South Haven/Grand Haven/Muskegon pier reports were slow or below average in September 2023.

**Conditions (backtest summary for the week before today; live data was not available)**
- Buoy surface water: St. Joseph 64 F, South Haven 66 F, Grand Haven 67 F, Muskegon 67 F, all flat over the week.
- Satellite surface water near the piers: about 67 F at all four, +0 to +1 F in the last three days.
- Upwelling wind (N to E, 8+ mph): Grand Haven 34 h over the week and 0 h in the last three days; Muskegon 41 h and 0 h; St. Joseph 16 h and 0 h; South Haven 19 h and 0 h.

## Caveats
- The reports are a week or more old, and Muskegon's are nearly four weeks old. Treat the ratings as a guide.
- Conditions were a backtest summary, not live readings. I don't have a three-day forecast or the modeled pierhead cold-layer depth, so I can't say whether a cold-water push is coming.
- Water temperatures are measured buoy or satellite values; they are not modeled pierhead values.
- The ratings for Muskegon and South Haven are low-confidence, since neither port has a recent pier-specific salmon report.
